newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romania to launch new 50,000 lei banknote.
newsitem.headline: Romania to launch new 50,000 lei banknote.

text.p: Romania's central bank will officially launch on Saturday its new 50,000 lei (about $15) banknote, which will go into circulation in the coming months.
Plans for the new note, which bears the face of 20th century composer George Enescu, have been delayed for over a year by public fears that bigger banknotes mean higher inflation.
The current highest denomination note is 10,000 lei, created in 1994 to cope with rising printing costs and bulging wallets.
The leu is officially quoted at 3,155/65 to the dollar but private exchange houses trade it at around 3,550. Year-on-year inflation rose to 40.3 percent in July from 27.8 at end-1995.
Like many post-communist currencies the leu suffered a stunning depreciation after the bloody 1989 revolution.
In the era of Stalinist dictator Nicolae Ceausescu the leu was set at 21 to the dollar and each leu was worth 100 bani. Bani coins have long disappeared.
The net average wage was 333,797 lei ($105) in July. -- Bucharest Newsroom 40-1 3120264
